Jalen Green doesn't think taking on more of a playmaker role will change his game.

"Same me, just getting guys involved a little more," Green said. "Making the right reads. If I'm making the right read, it's going to help my offensive game, too. It would be an even thing, but I've always been a good playmaker. I can make the right read sometimes. Sometimes, bad results, but I'm trying to find the right read in general. Step in the right direction. It's not that I can't pass the ball. It's just, let's make the better, the right reads."

Green is entering his second season with the Phoenix Suns looking to expand his game by simply being himself and making the correct decision based on how they're being defended.

"He's going to have the ball more," Suns coach Jordan Ott said. "We saw it as the season progressed, he's got more comfortable in our system, his system, but just make the right read. It's not shoot, pass, do, just make the right read."

Phoenix Suns begin training camp ahead of 2026-27 season. See photos

Green, 24, has averaged just 3.3 assists in his five NBA seasons. He managed just 2.8 a game last season, but Green only played 32 games due to a recurring left hamstring injury.

He remained in Phoenix for most of the offseason to return to full strength and work on improving his overall game with playmaking being one aspect of it.

"It's completely voluntary and he chose to live here and stay here and work out in this facility," Ott said. "He could still live here, stay here and work out somewhere else. We proved to him the building was a helpful place for him, but he has to make the commitment. He did. And we felt it (Tuesday). You'll see it when he plays. I think just think the understanding of reps that he was able to take on the floor was a big piece this summer, but the off-court work, what he's able to do in the weight room, just a consistent weight-room approach, will definitely help him."

Green spent time this summer with two-time NBA MVP Steve Nash to work on improving his playmaker skills.

One of league's greatest point guards ever, Nash led the league in assists five times. He's sixth all-time in career assists with 10,335.

Nash, who starred for the Suns during the early 2000s, took on a senior adviser role with the team last season.

"The pacing, just being able to read the game a little bit better," Green said. "Hearing from somebody of that caliber, being able to sit down and actually watch a workout and critique you as you go, that sticks with you. Just being able to hear him, how he breaks the game down, how he sees it, helps a lot."

Green isn't being asked to play like Nash.

The Suns are just looking for him to stay aggressive and read the play that should lead to either a good shot or pass.

"Make the right play, continuously put yourself in a threat position, which, again, we're going to continue to stress the paint," Ott said. "He can get there. And then when the defender comes, make the right play, when the defender doesn't come, go ahead and be aggressive. So just the evolution of his time in the NBA."

This shift could help relieve Devin Booker from shouldering too much of the playmaker duties so he can look to score even more.

Booker paced the Suns in points per game at 26.1 and assists at six a game last season, but he has seen a decline in his shot attempts since the 2021-22 season, when he hoisted a career-high 20.9 shots a game in averaging 26.8 points a game.

2022-23 season – 20.1 FGAs (career-high 27.8 PPG).

"The game is position-less now," Booker said. "I even talked about what the addition of Miles (Bridges), another person that can make plays. I think everybody on the court needs to be able to have those abilities. Frees up everybody. Makes it a free-flow offense. You learn with experience. You learn by being thrown in the fire, being trusted with those responsibilities and we've been seeing it in camp already with them."

articles.title: Em palestra promovida pela PUC-Campinas, Nina Silva | G1
articles.standfirst: Executiva de tecnologia e CEO defendeu a inclusão como elemento essencial para a criação de novos mercados e modelos de desenvolvimento
articles.summary: Executiva de tecnologia e CEO defendeu a inclusão como elemento essencial para a criação de novos mercados e modelos de desenvolvimento
articles.body:
Em palestra promovida pela PUC-Campinas, Nina Silva destaca diversidade — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação: PUC - Campinas

A relação entre inovação, diversidade e desenvolvimento econômico esteve no centro da palestra de Nina Silva, realizada nesta sexta-feira (18), durante o Campinas Innovation Week, em evento promovido pela PUC-Campinas e a FEAC. Com o tema “Tecnologia, Impacto Social e Negócios do Futuro: A Força da Diversidade na Economia”, a executiva de tecnologia, CEO do movimento Black Money e investidora-anjo abordou a necessidade de ampliar a participação de diferentes grupos sociais na construção de soluções e negócios inovadores.

Em palestra realizada no Green Stage, Nina afirmou que a presença de diferentes perspectivas é fundamental para ampliar discussões, estimular novas ideias e permitir a exploração de mercados que ainda não são plenamente atendidos.

“A diversidade é fundamental para que as cabeças se abram e, principalmente, novos mercados sejam explorados” - Nina Silva, CEO do movimento Black Money e executiva de tecnologia

Participaram também da mesa a Profa. Dra. Camila Brasil Gonçalves Campos, coordenadora do Departamento de Relações Externas (DRE) da PUC-Campinas e Lina Pimentel, diretora socioeducativa da FEAC, que colaboraram com a discussão colocando o ponto de vista universitário e da atuação da FEAC em Campinas.

Em palestra promovida pela PUC-Campinas, Nina Silva destaca diversidade

Nina lembrou que a busca por inclusão é resultado de movimentos sociais construídos ao longo de décadas e séculos e envolve diferentes grupos historicamente excluídos. Na avaliação dela, o desafio atual está em transformar o debate em políticas e ações capazes de modificar estruturas sociais e econômicas.

“Quando essa pauta é apenas uma pauta de discurso, a gente discute na academia, no âmbito privado e no âmbito público, mas não temos os poderes organizados e oxigenando, não conseguimos construir estratos sociais que realmente façam sentido para que essas políticas sejam incorporadas”, disse.

A executiva também chamou a atenção para mudanças recentes no cenário corporativo internacional e para o que classificou como uma regressão no diálogo sobre diversidade. Segundo Nina, empresas multinacionais que anteriormente lideravam iniciativas nessa área passaram, em alguns casos, a rever suas posições diante de mudanças políticas e de prioridades relacionadas ao capital.

“As desigualdades são estruturantes, estão nas estruturas, mas as soluções não estão sendo criadas de maneira estrutural”, afirmou.

Dados, inteligência artificial e diversidade

Ao abordar os avanços tecnológicos, Nina Silva também destacou a relação entre dados, comportamentos humanos e inteligência artificial. Segundo ela, os dados utilizados pelas tecnologias são, em grande medida, registros de comportamentos, relações e experiências humanas. Por isso, a diversidade de pessoas envolvidas na coleta, análise e desenvolvimento dessas tecnologias é fundamental para evitar que determinados contextos sociais e culturais fiquem de fora.

“Nossos dados simplesmente são comportamentos humanos. O que a gente lê? A gente lê nossos comportamentos. Armazenamos comportamentos e relações. E esses são os dados”, afirmou.

Ao relacionar o debate sobre diversidade ao ambiente de inovação, Nina Silva destacou ainda a necessidade de discutir a soberania tecnológica e financeira do Brasil. Segundo ela, ferramentas como a inteligência artificial representam avanços importantes na forma como tecnologias são disponibilizadas, mas parte significativa dessas estruturas ainda precisa evoluir no país e com pessoas à frente.

“Não existe inovação sem pessoas”, afirmou.

Ela também alertou para o risco de uma nova dependência tecnológica caso o país apenas utilize ferramentas desenvolvidas por outras sociedades, sem ampliar sua capacidade de produzir conhecimento e tecnologia. “Para que a gente construa modelos nossos de inovação, precisamos que a sociedade brasileira esteja na pauta dessa criação. E só estão na pauta da criação os que estão realmente incluídos, economicamente, financeiramente e socialmente falando”, destacou.

A executiva encerrou sua reflexão defendendo que a inclusão também precisa abrir espaço para que novas gerações possam ampliar as possibilidades de futuro, especialmente para grupos historicamente sub-representados.

“Eu quero ser a última geração de primeiros da minha família”, afirmou Nina, ao defender a construção de futuros desejáveis em lugar de limitar as possibilidades àquilo que é considerado apenas possível.

Confira a entrevista na íntegra, feita com Nina Silva:

Gostaria que você falasse um pouco sobre o tema que será tratado nesse painel de hoje

“Bom, primeiro gostaria de agradecer o convite do FEAC, também da PUC-Campinas, ainda tratando de dois temas que, para mim, são essenciais: inovação e diversidade. No momento em que diversidade está extremamente sensível nas pautas, tanto de política, quanto também nas pautas acadêmicas, nas pautas corporativas, a gente precisa manter uma resistência e precisa manter um trabalho para que diversidade saia desse lugar teórico do quase e realmente retome um lugar de protagonismo, de transformação social. E a inovação é uma grande porta para que isso aconteça. Então, a minha fala vai ser sobre isso: como processos realmente inovadores precisam de inovação, sustentabilidade e impacto. E diversidade entra nesse contexto, porque falas e comportamentos similares não trazem discussões, não trazem fomento, não trazem riqueza à mesa. Então, a diversidade é fundamental para que as cabeças se abram e, principalmente, novos mercados sejam explorados, até mesmo para grandes empresas e mercados já existentes.”

A inovação ainda é um tema novo, no sentido de se tornar popular. Por outro lado, temos um tema que já vem sendo debatido há muito tempo, que é a questão de dar visibilidade à diversidade. Existe uma parcela de discursos sem ações concretas. Como é que tem sido essa evolução que você tem percebido? Esse espaço, de fato, tem sido ampliado nos últimos anos? Ou ainda há uma barreira entre discurso e prática?

“Ganhamos, de 2015 a 2020, penetrando principalmente na parte da pandemia, uma visibilidade sobre o tema de diversidade e inclusão dentro das empresas. Só que o tema de diversidade e inclusão é uma pauta político-social de muitos e muitos anos, de décadas, de séculos de trabalho de movimentos sociais. E aí a gente está falando de vários grupos que são excluídos historicamente. A gente está falando de população preta, uma população majoritária no país que embasou o tratar capitalismo na sociedade brasileira. Foi a sociedade escravocrata que trouxe a possibilidade de fomento à riqueza para uma industrialização e o advento do capitalismo na sociedade brasileira. Então, nós estamos no cerne dessa desigualdade, no lugar da exclusão. E não no lugar do protagonismo do beneficiário e da beneficiada.”

“E aí a gente tem também outros grupos sociais, mulheres enquanto o lugar de propriedade que nos foi colocado historicamente. E a falta dessa inserção no mercado de trabalho proposital para a distinção de funções familiares e contextos sociais e grupos como a LGBTQIAPN+, que é uma sigla muito extensa para a gente botar dentro de uma única caixinha, mas que, da mesma forma, é colocado de maneira excludente.”

“Então, nós temos movimentos de resistência e de transgressão de anos e de séculos que começam a ganhar voz não no protagonismo de políticas estruturantes. E esse é o maior problema. Porque quando essa pauta é uma pauta apenas de discurso , a gente discute na academia, no âmbito privado, no âmbito público, mas a gente não tem os poderes organizados e oxigenando, Não conseguimos construir estratos sociais que realmente façam sentido para que essas políticas sejam incorporadas tanto no âmbito público quanto no âmbito privado.”

“Então, houve uma regressão, porque estava-se iniciando um diálogo no âmbito corporativo e aí mudanças políticas, mudanças de objetivos em relação ao capital mudou, políticas polarizadas foram ainda mais constituídas, e não só no Brasil, mas no mundo.”

“E essas multinacionais que antes estavam encabeçando esse diálogo, inserindo no Brasil, começaram a negar esse diálogo por conta de uma pauta política. E aí a gente vê que nós ficamos à mercê, porque as desigualdades são estruturantes, estão nas estruturas, mas as soluções não estão sendo criadas de maneira estrutural. Tem hora que vai ter regressão, tem hora que pode ser que tenha aparentemente um avanço.”

articles.title: He nearly won a U.S. Open and is now playing a new kind of competitive golf
articles.summary: John Peterson was a local qualifier who nearly won the U.S.
articles.body:
It was never about invitations to the fanciest clubs, the biggest sponsorships or the nicest cars.

In fact, for a time it seemed he would be remembered most as a side-door entrant: someone who didn't mind gritting his teeth and grinding out par after par against more talented players, despite a gap in raw ability that was evident even to him.

"In a nutshell… I have felt like I have done more with less than most," Peterson told GOLF.com Tuesday from his truck, en route to pick up supplies for his farm in Texas. "I think that's probably what I'm most proud about when I look back on my golf career."

Like everything else, Peterson's pride came the hard way. He was once one of the best collegiate golfers in the world, winning the 2011 NCAA individual title at LSU , only to emerge from his championship glow and find no guaranteed pathway to the PGA Tour. After failing at Q School and nearly going broke chasing Monday qualifiers and mini-tour starts, Peterson became one of the best underdog stories in the game: a local and sectional qualifier who stood over a birdie putt on the 72nd hole of the 2012 U.S. Open at Olympic Club that would have tied the clubhouse lead. (He lagged it to a foot instead, securing a tie for fourth and a spot in the next year's Masters.) Then he shifted into life as one of the Tour's preeminent everymen, making 91 starts over a handful of seasons. And then came another life change, this time as a pro golf retiree. He lingered on the fringes of the game for a while ( and retired twice! ) before settling down on his farm in Texas with his family.

Peterson has built a new life in the years since. He's the father of four kids, the eldest of whom is 8. He's a business owner, running Westoplex Garage, a Fort Worth company that installs automatic gates, overhead doors and epoxy floors. And he's a casual golfer for the first time in his life, logging roughly 20 rounds a year and, eventually, regaining his amateur status.

"I used to play 20 times in a month," Peterson says with a chuckle. "Golf is just a hobby at this point, and really not even that."

Still, parts of the pro experience lingered in his consciousness. Peterson had been a great golfer, but he had never represented the U.S. in a team event. He was left off the 2011 U.S. Walker Cup team after the best season of his life at LSU, and he never got close to wearing the stars and stripes again.

Peterson thought he might live with that "what if?" forever, and that he might never know what it was like to play for the red, white and blue.

Next week, Peterson will be part of an American side competing against the rest of the world in the annual Bridges Cup , an elite mid-amateur, Ryder Cup-style competition held this year at Trump Turnberry in Scotland.

While his playing time has dwindled, Peterson has worked to sharpen his game. This summer, he teed it up in the Jones Cup, the Sunnehanna Amateur and the Southern Amateur. Earlier this year, he also competed as a wild card in Your Golf Tour , the YouTube circuit co-founded by George and Wesley Bryan, which drew millions of views.

"I'd spent… nine years playing pro golf, some of it at the highest level in the world, and never been recognized in an airport," he said. "The week after that thing came out, I got stopped three times in the Atlanta airport."

The buzz has faded a bit in the months since, but the experience reinforced something in Peterson's mind: golf is a game of shared experiences. Next week, when he dons the American uniform for the first time, he'll be reminded of something else. Even when your pro career ends, those experiences remain.

"It's not the same, but I still get to wear the red, white, and blue, which is going to be awesome," Peterson said.

articles.title: Public control of water not enough, Green deputy leader says
articles.summary: Rachel Millward says her party would nationalise water companies to reverse years of “radical underinvestment".
articles.body:
Green Party co-deputy leader Rachel Millward has said her party would nationalise water companies in England and Wales, criticising Prime Minister Andy Burnham's plans to bring them under public control as "vague".

Millward told the BBC the country's water system was an "absolutely unmitigated disaster", arguing there had been "radical underinvestment" over decades.

She said Burnham's plan, which involves removing limits on government ownership of shares in water companies and giving mayors more powers to scrutinise them, did not go far enough.

The Green Party of England and Wales has long called for public ownership of water companies, describing privatisation as a failed experiment.

In its 2024 manifesto, the party estimated that nationalising water companies and the five biggest retail energy firms would cost £30bn over the five years of a parliament.

Last year, the government estimated that nationalising the water industry would cost approximately £100bn.

Millward is expected to make a speech about the party's latest policy on nationalising water companies - and how to pay for it - at the Green Party conference in Brighton this weekend.

It comes as the government considers the option of nationalising Thames Water, which is facing a severe financial crisis.

Ahead of the conference, Millward did a round of interviews with local BBC radio stations across England.

Under the leadership of Zack Polanski, the party's brand of "eco-populism" has posed a challenge to Labour on the left of British politics.

Labour's polling numbers have improved markedly in recent months, suggesting Burnham may be winning back some supporters that had drifted towards Polanski's party.

In her interviews, Millward said the party had had a "historic successful year" by winning a by-election in Gorton and Denton, and making significant gains in May's local elections.

She told BBC Radio Newcastle if it had not been for the rise of the Greens, then Sir Keir Starmer - who was ousted as prime minister by his own MPs - would still be in office.

"We can take the credit for that really," she said.

Millward said Labour's rhetoric had "shifted in our direction" under Burnham.

Going forward she said the Greens would push the Labour government to go further and continue calling for rent controls, nationalisation of water companies and wealth taxes.

But Millward faced some tough questions on local issues, some of which she wasn't able to answer.

She was asked by BBC Radio WM about the bin strikes in Birmingham, where a minority coalition of Liberal Democrats, Greens and independents run the council.

She said she hadn't "been given enough information to answer that question" and apologised several times.

"I'm sorry it's not in my briefing, it should have been," she said. "I'm happy to come on another time and chat about it."

These BBC local radio rounds can be tricky, with presenters often asking about issues in their patches.

Millward seemed most comfortable on national topics, arguing the Greens "have the power to set the agenda for this government" and hold Burnham to account.

The Greens have five MPs and hundreds of councillors across the country.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski is currently contesting the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, which will take place next week. A full list of candidates is available on the BBC website .

articles.title: Jayden Reed sends encouraging message after Packers place him on injured reserve
articles.summary: Jayden Reed is facing a murky recovery after a neck injury abruptly ended his involvement in the Green Bay Packers’ 20-17 overtime win over the New York Jets...
articles.body:
Jayden Reed is facing a murky recovery after a neck injury abruptly ended his involvement in the Green Bay Packers ' 20-17 overtime win over the New York Jets . The wide receiver went down during the second offensive play and was taken away on a backboard before remaining overnight at a hospital in New York.

Reed had agreed to a three year, $50 million extension with Green Bay in April, but the team does not yet know when he will be able to return. James Palmer said on NFL on Prime that there is no established timeline for Reed, with the possibility of a season ending absence still on the table as the Packers proceed with maximum caution.

The 26-year-old's potential absence for the remainder of the season would be a major setback for the Green Bay Packers offense. Adam Schefter later confirmed on X that Green Bay is placing Reed on injured reserve because of his neck injury, leaving him sidelined indefinitely.

Jayden Reed on his injury with the Packers

Despite the difficult circumstances, the Packers star offered an encouraging message to his followers on Instagram, writing, "God will use the unusual to do the unexpected… 11 out."

Reed's positive mindset gives the Green Bay Packers something to hold onto as the team continues dealing with a growing list of injuries. Matt LaFleur said Reed's teammates were encouraged after he regained feeling throughout his body earlier in the week, but the Packers remain committed to taking a careful approach with his recovery.

With Reed unavailable, Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are expected to take on more responsibility in the slot, adding another challenge for an offense already dealing with major problems along the offensive line. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele is also out for the season after suffering a patellar tendon tear, leaving Green Bay with even more uncertainty up front.

articles.title: Phil Mickelson Opens Up On His Rehab Stint
articles.summary: Phil Mickelson checked himself into a treatment facility earlier this year as he dealt with “family trauma and addiction,” according to a statement from his...
articles.body:
Phil Mickelson checked himself into a treatment facility earlier this year as he dealt with "family trauma and addiction," according to a statement from his representatives provided to multiple media outlets .

The disclosure adds context for Mickelson's prolonged absence from professional golf during a 2026 season in which the six-time major champion was almost absent from competition.

Mickelson, 56, is no longer at the facility. He played just once on the LIV Golf schedule , appearing at the league's event in South Africa, and missed all four major championships. He had exemptions that would have allowed him to compete in three of them.

His absence initially came with considerably less detail. Mickelson cited a "family health matter" when he stepped away from LIV Golf early in the season. In April, when confirming he would not play in the Masters, he said that he and his family were dealing with a "personal health matter."

More information emerged as the year progressed.

In June, reports indicated that Mickelson had lost his membership at The Farms Golf Club, his longtime club in Rancho Santa Fe, following an allegation that he made inappropriate, non-consensual contact with a female employee. The Farms did not publicly identify Mickelson, but the club confirmed that an incident had taken place and that a member had been removed.

Mickelson's attorney denied the allegations and said that "any misunderstanding has been cleared up." At the time, his attorney again said Mickelson was focused on a family health matter.

Weeks later, Ashley Perez, professional golfer Pat Perez's ex-wife, publicly described several alleged incidents involving Mickelson. Among her accusations was a claim that Mickelson propositioned her for sex in 2015.

After publishing Perez's account, Mickelson's attorney released another statement that offered a clearer indication of what Mickelson had been dealing with privately, saying he was in recovery and had the support of his wife, Amy.

"Recovery is not a straight line," the statement said. "Throughout their 35-year relationship, his wife, Amy Mickelson, has supported Mr. Mickelson and their family with extraordinary grace, unwavering love and the belief that people are measured not only by their failures, but by what they do to make them right."

The statement continued by saying Mickelson's priority was becoming "the husband, father, and man his family deserves," while asking that the family's private health matters remain private.

Mickelson has previously spoken publicly about his struggles with gambling addiction, making addiction a subject he had addressed well before the latest disclosure about his treatment.

A Major-Championship Streak Comes to an End

These developments have unfolded amid a dramatic shift in Mickelson's presence in professional golf. Once one of the sport's most recognizable and consistently discussed players, he has become increasingly limited in his competitive appearances. At the same time, a series of controversies and personal issues have drawn attention away from his play.

The 2026 season represented the most striking example yet. Mickelson failed to appear in any of golf's four majors for the first time since 1989, ending a run that stretched across more than three decades.

Now, a statement from his representatives fills in part of what happened during those months away. What had previously been described publicly as a family or personal health matter included Mickelson entering treatment for family trauma and addiction. At the same time, his golf career was effectively placed on hold.

articles.title: 2026 Bank of Utah Championship scores, live updates, tee times for Thursday's Round 1
articles.summary: Welcome to the Bank of Utah Championship, the PGA Tour event in Ivins, Utah. For all the Thursday live updates, keep it right here with Golfweek.
articles.body:
It's one of 45 tournament's on the PGA Tour in 2026. It's the second of eight FedEx Cup Fall series events.

Welcome to the Bank of Utah Championship , a now three-year-old event in Ivins, Utah, in the southern part of that state.

Black Desert Golf Course provides the stunning landscape for this event. It was the final golf course designed by Tom Weiskopf .

For all the Thursday live updates, keep it right here with Golfweek .

Photos: Black Desert Resort for the Bank of Utah Championship

Bank of Utah Championship 2026 leaderboard

Keep tabs on the PGA Tour's Bank of Utah Championship all week for the latest scores.

Bank of Utah Championship 2026 tee times

See all the pairings and start times at Black Desert Resort for Thursday's first round. The first group is off at 7:35 a.m. local, which is 9:35 a.m. ET.

How to watch the Bank of Utah Championship 2026, TV information

PGA Tour Live on ESPN+ : 9:45 a.m. ET - 8 p.m. ET

PGA Tour Radio on Sirius XM: 2 p.m. ET - 8 p.m. ET

Key number for the Bank of Utah Championship

11. That's how many under the winner has played the par 4s at Black Desert Resort in the previous two editions of this tournament. The two winners at this event have a par-4 birdie or better percentage of 34.09 percent compared to only 21.15 percent by the rest of the field.

Utah's favorite son is making his tournament debut finally. Finau, 37, is a six-time PGA Tour winner and serves as an ambassador of the Korn Ferry Tour event in Utah but he's been unable to play here the past two years. "To have a PGA Tour event in Utah and now to be participating in it on this stage for a home crowd, I'm really excited about it," he said Wednesday. Finau went to West High School in Salt Lake City and won the Utah State Amateur Championship in 2006.

What's the prize money at the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship?

The total purse for the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship is $6 million, the same as it was in 2025. The winner of the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship receives $1.08 million, or 18 percent of the total purse.

Who are the past winners of the Bank of Utah Championship?

In 2024, Matt McCarty posted a final-round 4-under 67 on Sunday and win the inaugural Black Desert Championship in Ivins, Utah, in just his second start on the PGA Tour.

In 2025, Michael Brennan bombed his way around the course to win in just his third PGA Tour start.

Where is the Bank of Utah Championship played?

Black Desert Resort opened in 2023 and quickly rocketed up several of the Golfweek's Best rankings:

T-30 in the top 200 resort golf courses in the U.S.

T-38 in the top 100 public-access golf courses in the U.S.

101 in the top 200 modern golf courses in the U.S.

The golf course plays as a par 71 and measures 7,421 yards for the pros. The property has dramatic lava rock outcroppings all over. The National Park Service reports that the latest volcanic eruption was 32,000 years ago from what is now Snow Canyon State Park, just a couple of miles north of the golf course. The site for Black Desert looks much more like something to be found in Hawaii, minus the ocean views, but with plenty of promise.

Weather forecast for 2026 Bank of Utah Championship

articles.title: Matthew Golden Left Heartbroken by Tough Packers News
articles.summary: The blows just keep on coming to Matthew Golden and the Green Bay Packers, who are only 1-2 after three weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Even in their lone win...
articles.body:
The blows just keep on coming to Matthew Golden and the Green Bay Packers , who are only 1-2 after three weeks of the 2026 NFL season.

Even in their lone win thus far against the New York Jets in Week 2, the Packers didn't look particularly convincing, and making matters worse was the neck injury suffered by wide receiver Jayden Reed during that contest .

Reed is done for the rest of the season, leaving a significant hole in the team's Jordan Love-led passing attack. Among those counted upon by Green Bay to step up and help cover the void left by Reed is rising wideout Golden, who has led the Packers in receiving yards in each of the last two games.

Matthew Golden Speaks up on Reed After Latter's Season-Ending Neck Injury

Talking to reporters, Golden expressed his thoughts on Reed, who has helped him in more ways than one in adjusting to life in the pros.

"I'm kind of hurt to because me and J Reed got tight. I seen how much work he put in this offseason. The impact he had on me coming into my second year… I feel like we have a good connection," the former Texas Longhorns star wide receiver Golden said on Wednesday, via Vince Lovergine of WLUK-TV FOX 11 .

With Reed out, Golden can be expected to get even more looks downfield. He is coming off a breakout game with 100 receiving yards and a touchdown (his career's first in the regular season) on five catches and 12 targets, albeit in a 35-14 loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field in Week 3.

Golden will look to keep it going in Week 4, as Green Bay aims to get back to its winning ways and avoid a 1-3 record when the team takes on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road this coming Sunday.

Selected by Green Bay in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Golden has 253 receiving yards and a touchdown on 15 receptions through three games this season.

articles.title: Here comes Kevin Zeitler to save the day
articles.summary: One veteran can’t really save the Packers’ entire season on his own, can he?
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers desperately needed help on the offensive line — particularly at guard. There, out on the open market, was veteran Kevin Zeitler , finally healthy after rehabbing a quad injury during the offseason. Packers fans had spent the last few weeks theorizing about the Wisconsin native and former Badger All-American coming in to save the day, at least at one position on the line; thankfully, the Packers recognized the fit and made it happen.

Is Zeitler really a panacea for everything plaguing the Packers' offense? Certainly not. But if he can stabilize one of those interior spots and just not let free rushers through on damn near every play , that will go a long way to helping Jordan Love lead a competent offense.

Meanwhile, you can put to bed any projection of an outside zone running scheme with the recent changes up front. With the line likely to eventually consist of Aaron Banks or Laken Tomlinson at left guard, Zeitler at right guard, and Anthony Belton at tackle, the Packers will almost assuredly be back on board with the power run game. Hopefully that sets up well for a big back like Kaleb Johnson , even if he played in a zone scheme in college.

Zeitler alone won't save the Packers' season. The other players and the coaching staff need to do their part. But it does feel like Zeitler's arrival could be a catalyst that dramatically changes the trajectory of this team's 2026 campaign.

For Packers and Kevin Zeitler, Here's Why It's Dream Fit | SI.com It's not hard to explain: Zeitler is from Waukesha, just outside of Milwaukee. He played at Wisconsin. Now he has a chance to wind down his career in his home state.

New Packers OL Kevin Zeitler already making case to start in Week 4 | Packers Wire It's hard to imagine even a rusty Zeitler playing worse than Jacob Monk has in his three games so far this year.

Meanwhile, Zeitler explains when the Packers contacted him:

Veteran linemen expected to 'settle things down' for Packers up front | Packers.com Between Zeitler and Laken Tomlinson, who took #1 reps at left guard on Wednesday, the team could have a new-look interior line as early as this Sunday.

Green Bay Packers offensive line must give Jordan Love time to be himself | Packersnews.com That line has to do enough to let Love cook, because the Packers still can't rely on the run game right now. But if they can at least keep Love from getting pressured quickly all the time, he's plenty good enough to lead a solid offense.

articles.summary: The Alfred Dunhill Links Championship is played over three courses – Carnoustie, Kingsbarns and St Andrews with the Old Course hosting the final day – and also incorporates a team event with a number of former sports stars and celebrities paired with the professionals
articles.body:
The 36-year-old has played only five DP World Tour events - the last in 2023 - and teed off less than 24 hours after finishing second in the Tartan Tour's Duddingston Classic having received a sponsor's invite earlier this week.

He had a remarkable back nine at Carnoustie, where an eagle at the par-five 12th was the catalyst to play five holes in six under par.

With a solitary birdie on the front nine he finished with a blemish-free seven under.

"It's easy to get yourself up for this event. I played Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday [at Duddingston] but I've played a lot here in the past," said Stewart on his lack of a practice round.

"Just delighted to be able to be part of the event. I feel right at home with links golf. I just played really nice all day."

The tournament is played over three courses - Carnoustie, Kingsbarns and St Andrews with the Old Course hosting the final day - and also incorporates a team event with a number of former sports stars and celebrities paired with the professionals.

Matt Fitzpatrick, who arrived in Scotland off the back of his fourth win of the year at the Open de France, shot a four-under 68 at Carnoustie, with Ryder Cup team-mate Tommy Fleetwood two under at the same course.

Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka was three under after a 69 at Carnoustie, while defending champion and home favourite Bob MacIntyre was one under at the same course.

Lee Westwood and Ian Poulter, on their first DP World Tour appearances in almost four years, shot one under at St Andrews and level par at Carnoustie respectively with fellow LIV golfer Bubba Watson also level at Carnoustie.

On a day when Matt Fitzpatrick began his quest for a fifth win of the year, Robert MacIntyre reacted furiously to a drone and Lee Westwood and Ian Poulter made a DP World Tour return after an absence of almost four years, it was a player from outside the world's top 900 that stole the show at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

Scotland's Michael Stewart, ranked 979, shot 65 to sit at seven under after outscoring a big-name field to share the lead at the end of round one.

It gave the Scot a share of the lead after round one, with Australia's Jack Buchanan.

Stewart, 36, has played only five events on the main European circuit - the last in 2023 - and teed off less than 24 hours after finishing second in the Tartan Tour's Duddingston Classic having received a sponsor's invite this week.

However, after making a solitary birdie on the front nine, an eagle on the par-five 12th proved to be the catalyst for him the play the next five holes in six under after the turn.

"It's easy to get yourself up for this event. I played Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday [at Duddingston], straight here. I've played here a lot in the past and just delighted to be part of the event.

"I grew up on a links course. I played nice all day to be honest. Lots of fairways, lots of greens and then on the back, the putter got hot."

Stewart's remarkable back nine at Carnoustie and Buchanan's equally impressive score at Kingsbarns, was in contrast to several eye-catching moments in the team event featuring former sports stars and celebrities, who were paired with the professionals.

However, ex-Real Madrid and Wales winger Gareth Bale did at least provide instantly shareable social media content when his ball found the roof of the Jigger Inn, teeing off on the 17th at St Andrews - one of three courses utilised to stage the tournament.

South Africa's MJ Daffue and Casey Jarvis are a stroke off the lead on the professional leaderboard, while Fitzpatrick, who was victorious at the French Open last week, signed for a four-under 68 to sit three shots adrift.

Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka was three under after a 69 at Carnoustie, a shot better off than Tommy Fleetwood, while defending champion MacIntyre was one under at the same course.

MacIntyre was also spoken to by officials after losing his temper because of a drone flying above him on the par-three eighth, his penultimate hole of the day.

"It drives me insane. I've had previous for it," he said.

"I asked [the rules official] twice previous to the shot on the eighth about the drone. I can't say anything just now.

"He's obviously heard me swear a few times straight at the camera guy. We'll see what the TD [tournament director] has got to say."

Westwood is at one under, with Poulter at level par on their first appearances on the DP World Tour since January 2023, having made controversial switches to LIV Golf in 2022.

articles.title: Blackburn calls on TN to ‘bring back’ electric chair after botched Christa Pike execution
articles.summary: Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) on Thursday called on Tennessee to reintroduce the electric chair for executions after death-row prisoner Christa Pike survived two lethal injections the day before. Blachburn, who is the GOP nominee in the Volunteer State’s gubernatorial race, called the botched execution “tragic” and said it prolonged the grief process for victims in…
articles.body:
Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) on Thursday called on Tennessee to reintroduce the electric chair for executions after death-row prisoner Christa Pike survived two lethal injections the day before.

Blachburn, who is the GOP nominee in the Volunteer State’s gubernatorial race, called the botched execution “tragic” and said it prolonged the grief process for victims in this case.

“While there should be a thorough review of what happened and why the process failed, the answer is simple: bring back the electric chair and deliver justice for these victims swiftly,” the senator wrote on social media . “As your governor, I will do just that.”

Pike was convicted of first-degree murder after she confessed to the 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville, Tenn.

Prosecutors said Slemmer was lured to an abandoned steam plant near the University of Tennessee Agricultural campus and beaten, tortured and killed by Pike and the inmate’s then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp. Shipp was not eligible for the death penalty since he was 17 at the time of the crime, and he was sentenced to life in prison and denied parole last year.

Following the state’s botched lethal injection process on Wednesday evening, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee (R) ordered Pike’s execution to be delayed until at least next year to allow for an independent investigation to take place.

Earlier this year, state executioners failed to execute death row inmate Tony Carruthers after they failed to find a vein for a lethal injection. Lee granted a one-year reprieve in this case.

Memphis City Council member Jerri Green, the Democratic nominee in the governor’s race, pushed back on Blackburn’s call to bring back the electric chair in a statement.

“There is a lack of transparency around drug testing, as well as qualified and ethical personnel—but the fact of the matter is: the death penalty has always been inhumane, expensive, and biased,” she wrote on social media . “And Marsha Blackburn wants to bring back one of the most cruel forms of capital punishment, the electric chair.”

Green noted she would “put a moratorium on all future executions” if elected to the state’s top office.

“If we say we are pro-life, that means we must be anti-death penalty,” the Democrat added.

Pike is the sole woman on Tennessee’s death row, and she would have been the first woman to be executed in the state in over 200 years.

Her scheduled execution was initially delayed by an 11th-hour stay order from the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which was later lifted by the Supreme Court. The high court’s three liberal justices dissented in this decision.

Advocacy groups called on the state to abolish the death penalty following the Wednesday botched execution attempt.

United Nations Human Rights Chief Volker Türk called on state authorities “not to pursue any further attempt to execute Pike” in a Thursday statement .

“The prolonged suffering — physical and mental — arising from multiple failed execution attempts is abhorrent, and cruel,” Türk said. “And there are key fair trial questions still unresolved.”

articles.title: Battle of the Bays features winless Buccaneers and struggling Packers
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3) need a victory even more than the Green Bay Packers (1-2) on Sunday.  At least Green Bay has quarterback Jordan Love.  Tampa B...
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — The Battle of the Bays features two struggling teams searching for an identity and a win.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3) need a victory even more than the Green Bay Packers (1-2) on Sunday. They're trying to avoid an 0-4 start because only one team in NFL history — the 1992 Chargers — overcame that to make the playoffs.

But 1-3 isn't much better so there's plenty of urgency for the Packers, who were booed at Lambeau Field following an embarrassing loss to Atlanta in their home opener last Thursday.

At least Green Bay has quarterback Jordan Love . Tampa Bay is turning to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels after Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb in a loss to Minnesota .

"For us, it's just trying to get a win," Bucs coach Todd Bowles said. "(Jalon Daniels) is not playing by himself. Everybody has to do their job. We've got to coach it the right way on both sides of the ball, including special teams. He's got to play and just do his job. We've got 21 other guys that (are) going to be out there playing with him, so he's not by himself. It's (a) nervous (feeling) but it's exciting at the same time because you get to see somebody play. No matter where you come from, your first NFL game has to come at some point, whether you're a first-round pick or whether you're a free agent. You've got to touch the field for the first time at some point, and then you've got to play. He's just got to play."

While the Buccaneers have a new quarterback, Love will have new faces blocking for him. The Packers have had to revamp their offensive line because of several injuries. They signed veteran guards Kevin Zeitler , Laken Tomlinson and Mekhi Becton this week.

"It's just a matter getting to work, seeing how fast those guys can pick up the offense," Love said of the recent additions. "I think at the end of the day, putting the best five out there and there's always going to be some competition in those positions, so do whatever the team feels best at that position."

When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox.

Against the spread: Packers 0-3; Buccaneers 0-3.

Last week: Packers lost to the Falcons 35-14; Buccaneers lost to the Vikings 23-16.

Last meeting: Buccaneers beat the Packers 34-20 on Dec. 17, 2023, in Green Bay.

Packers wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden vs. Buccaneers cornerbacks Zyon McCollum , Jacob Parrish and Benjamin Morrison . McCollum has allowed a passer rating of just 69.3 in the first three games. He'll be tested by Watson, who has 17 catches for 284 yards and four TDs.

Packers QB Jordan Love has 89 TD passes, tied with Tobin Rote for No. 5 in team history. Love has thrown multiple TD passes in each of the first three games, the first Packers QB to do so since Aaron Rodgers in 2020.

WR Christian Watson is the first Packers player with a TD catch in each of the first three games of the season since Davante Adams in 2018. Watson is the first Packers player with four TD receptions in the first three games since Jordy Nelson in 2016.

Watson is the first Packers player with 15-plus catches, 275-plus receiving yards and four-plus receiving TDs in the first three games of the season since WR James Lofton in 1983.

Safety Xavier McKinney had his 20th career interception last week.

Packers punter Daniel Whelan placed four punts inside the 20-yard line last week.

The Buccaneers are 0-3 for the first time since 2014.

Jalon Daniels will be the first backup quarterback to start for Tampa Bay since Ryan Fitzpatrick in 2018.

The Buccaneers allowed 230 total yards against Minnesota on Sunday, their fewest allowed in a game this season and the second-fewest overall since the start of the 2025 season.

WR Ted Hurst III had a 40-yard touchdown reception vs. Minnesota for his first career score.

OLB David Walker has two sacks in his first three career games.

Kicker Chase McLaughlin is 9 for 9 this season. He leads the NFL with 14 field goals of at least 50 yards since 2025.

articles.title: Phil Mickelson reportedly checked himself into treatment center for 'family trauma and addiction'
articles.summary: Phil Mickelson has been away from golf for months now while dealing with a "personal health matter" in his family.
articles.body:
Longtime PGA Tour star and LIV Golf member Phil Mickelson recently checked himself into an addiction treatment center amid his extended absence from the sport, according to multiple reports.

Mickelson reportedly checked himself in voluntarily, and is already out of the facility. He was "seeking treatment for family trauma and addiction," a representative for Mickelson told TMZ. Further specifics are not yet known.

Mickelson announced before the Masters in April that he was stepping away from golf due to a "personal health matter" in his family. He did not get into specifics, but he hasn't played anywhere since. He was briefly entered into the field at the PGA Championship in May , but withdrew and said he "unfortunately" could not play.

Mickelson was also accused of inappropriate conduct at The Farms Golf Club near San Diego earlier this year, and he's no longer a member at that club. Mickelson was accused of "nonconsensual and inappropriate physical conduct" by a female employee before a round. Mickelson's spokesman called it a "misunderstanding" that has "been cleared up."

Mickelson has been open about his gambling addiction in the past, too. A book released in 2023 even alleged that Mickelson has bet a total of at least $1 billion, and his losses reached as much as $100 million. He even allegedly bet on the 2012 Ryder Cup while he was on the team, though he's denied this, and his longtime gambling partner Billy Walters was convicted of insider trading in 2017. Mickelson had to forfeit almost $1 million in earnings gained through stock tips he received from Walters in the case.

Mickelson was once a dominant force on the PGA Tour. He won 45 times on Tour and has six major championship titles to his name, most recently at the PGA Championship in 2021. He was a driving force behind the creation of LIV Golf and subsequent feud within the sport, too. He drew plenty of criticism for comments he made about partnering with Saudi Arabia early on, though LIV Golf has since lost its funding from the country's Public Investment Fund. Mickelson played in just a single LIV Golf event last season.

With LIV Golf's future up in the air, and Mickelson still away from competitive golf dealing with off-course issues, it's unclear when he may return.

articles.title: Trump meme coin firm invites top buyers to ‘exclusive’ gala with the president
articles.summary: The firm managing President Trump’s $TRUMP meme coin announced it is hosting an “exclusive” gala for the top 185 holders of the coin, featuring the president as a speaker. “An evening with 3 Legends and President Donald J. Trump — plus a private meet & greet with a legend to be announced,” the description of…
articles.body:
The firm managing President Trump’s $TRUMP meme coin announced it is hosting an “exclusive” gala for the top 185 holders of the coin, featuring the president as a speaker.

“An evening with 3 Legends and President Donald J. Trump — plus a private meet & greet with a legend to be announced,” the description of the event read, adding, “No attendees will be granted a private meet & greet with the President.”

Trump’s meme coin website said the gala is planned for Nov. 22 at Trump National Golf Club in Washington with the “3 legends” expected to be announced before the event.

The webpage also included that the top 29 qualifying holders are eligible for an exclusive “VIP Reception” at the gala “with your favorite President and one of the Legends.”

A disclaimer in smaller font below stated, “There will be no private meetings with the President. No gifts will be accepted.”

An 18-karat Trump gold watch is promised for the top four holders of the coin.

To be eligible to attend, people must rank above 186th place on a leaderboard when the eligibility window ends on Nov. 12. The website said a user’s scoring will climb “the longer you hold” but warned that if someone dumps all of their $TRUMP coin, “you drop off all active leaderboards.”

In 2025, Trump hosted a similar gala at his golf club with more than 200 top investors in his meme coin — and a tour of the White House for the top 25 holders.

Meme coins — including $TRUMP — are defined by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as a type of crypto asset that are purchased for “entertainment, social interaction and cultural purposes” and have a value “driven primarily by market demand and speculation.”

The coins are cryptocurrencies that have no inherent value, often making them highly volatile assets.

Trump launched the coin before the beginning of his second term in an announcement post that garnered more than 100 million views.

The price of $TRUMP shot up by 550 percent to nearly $30 during its launch, and the market value of the coin was $30 billion on paper, according to CoinGecko . It sits at around $2 on Thursday, with the market value estimated at $580.88 million, but its value notably shot up when the webpage launched Wednesday.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) have called it a “ rug pull ” by Trump and asked the SEC to investigate the president’s ties to the coin.

The SEC clarified in February that meme coins are not a security, moving it to a case-by-case review by the agency to determine if legal action is necessary.

Democratic lawmakers have similarly slammed Trump for his crypto ventures following his financial disclosures revealing he raked in more than $500 million from World Liberty Financial, which he and his sons helped launch in 2024.

articles.title: Bears Pump Brakes on Kyler Gordon Return in New Revelation
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears divulged some previously unknown information on CB Kyler Gordon while also addressing his return timeline to game action. The post Bears Pu...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have cornerback Kyler Gordon back on the practice field, but that does not mean he will be heavily involved in the team's game plan right away.

Gordon's designation to the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list to begin the season means he is not even eligible for action against the New York Jets on Sunday, October 4.

The cornerback can return to the field against the Green Bay Packers in Week 5, though what kind of role he can/will play is going to depend on how quickly he can catch up to his teammates in terms of game-specific conditioning.

Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said as much during a press conference on Thursday, during which he also revealed that the team was aware of Gordon's practice return timeline long before the news broke publicly.

"Dennis Allen said he found out a week or two ago that Kyler Gordon would be back in the building and ready to return to practice this week," per a CHGO Bears report on social media. "DA said Gordon looked good yesterday, but the focus now is getting back into football shape."

Kyler Gordon's Return Provides Bears With Much-Needed Depth in Secondary

Gordon's return should prove significant for the Bears, assuming that the $40 million cornerback can recapture his 2024 form. He missed all but three games last season due to soft-tissue injuries like the calf strain that will rob him of at least the first four contests of the current campaign.

Chicago will undoubtedly put Gordon back into his primary position as the team's nickel cornerback, where he is the league's highest-paid player, which probably means that rookie Malik Muhammad will move into a reserve role on the outside.

However, Muhammad has shown the capability to play inside as well, so he will be something of a swing defensive back who can play multiple positions as needed.

Tyrique Stevenson , the Bears' second outside cornerback alongside Jaylon Johnson , is dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2. Stevenson played against the Eagles last Monday night, though Muhammad started in his place due to the injury.

Malik Muhammad May Replace Tyrique Stevenson as Bears' 2nd Outside CB Permanently After Kyler Gordon Return

Muhammad has played 31 more defensive snaps ( 134 ) than Stevenson ( 103 ) through three games.

Chicago's initial thinking when drafting Muhammad out of Texas in Round 4 back in April was that he might challenge Stevenson for the starting job as a rookie and could eventually take his place as the starter on the outside moving forward.

Stevenson is in the final year of his rookie contract and Chicago can potentially get similar, or even better, play from Muhammad on a rookie-scale deal for the next three years moving forward.

What Muhammad's stellar play, Stevenson's nagging muscle strain and Gordon's imminent return combine to create now is a situation in which Muhammad might usurp Stevenson's role on the outside permanently as soon as Gordon is fully healthy.

In the short term, it provides the Bears' secondary with some much-needed depth, which might last throughout the year assuming relative health.

It could also provide the Bears a chance to rest Stevenson until he is healthy and then shop him ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, as starting Muhammad and waiting for a compensatory pick from the NFL for Stevenson — should he leave next offseason in free agency — may prove less lucrative from an asset-acquisition perspective.

articles.title: Former Dolphins coach boldly compares Malik Willis to star QB
articles.summary: Former Miami Dolphins assistant coach Dave Shula has lofty praise for the team's starting quarterback, Malik Willis.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins may be off to a rough start to the 2026 season, but Dave Shula has plenty of optimism.

Shula is obviously best known as the son of legendary head coach Don Shula. However, the eldest son of the Shula family also coached the Dolphins as an assistant, serving as a quarterbacks and wide receivers coach between 1982-88 during the early portion of Dan Marino's career.

The 67-year-old Shula keeps close tabs on the current Dolphins regime, having lunch with head coach Jeff Hafley and ex-Dolphins coach Dave Wannstedt. One of the key players Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan brought in was none other than quarterback Malik Willis. Hafley and Sullivan are obviously very familiar with Willis, as he played as the backup quarterback over the past two seasons with the Green Bay Packers.

While Willis has faced his share of criticism during his first three starts with the Dolphins -- he has just one touchdown against two interceptions and hasn't produced a ton of yardage -- he does have a supporter in Shula.

"Another thing they did was bringing in Willis from Green Bay, so they knew him and his abilities," said Shula in a one-on-one interview with Dolphins Wire. "I remember seeing him last year playing, and I was very impressed with him, his production, what he was able to do. So hopefully, they'll build a team around him and continue when they get opportunities to bring in players. But the big thing will be developing the young guys, and that's their job in 2026, and to build a foundation and to go forward. Build a culture, and I'm sure they're on their way to doing that."

Willis had just six career starts before this season, something that Hafley recently made mention to reporters following their latest loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. In other words, Willis has never been a full-time starter and is really gaining true experience as a full-time starting quarterback for the first time in his career.

"I think sometimes we forget that this is (Malik Willis') first year really being a starting quarterback, which is way different than coming in at spot duty and playing a few games," said Hafley of Willis. "I thought he improved today and I'm excited to see the film."

When asked for a player style comparison for Willis, Hafley gave him lofty praise -- he compared him to Chicago Bears star quarterback Caleb Williams.

"Malik, I just remember watching him, I'm thinking of the Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has a lot of those same traits: physical, great arm, great arm talent," said Shula of Willis.

Shula hasn't coached in the NFL since he was the head coach of the Cincinnati Bengals from 1992 until 1996, but in more recent years he served as the wide receivers coach at his alma mater, Dartmouth. He's now returning as the president of his family's restaurant group, Shula's Restaurant Group . Shula previously served in the role for two decades from 1997 until 2018.

He's leading the expansion plans of the company, which includes Shula's American Kitchen in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, and an entry into Thomasville, Georgia, in 2027.

"It's great to be back," said Shula. "The company, obviously, I have a lot of stake in. I was here with Shula's for 22 years, from '97 through '18 on a day to day basis, and then went back up to got back into coaching at my alma mater, Dartmouth College, coached receivers for six years, and then came back and and talked to Mary Anne shula — who's the CEO and my dad's widow — this summer, and she was looking for somebody to come in and take over the president's role. I was happy to want to have the opportunity and something that I obviously have a passion for and want to see our name represented well and be back in the business."

articles.title: Greens back North East data centre pause and no Hartlepool nuclear
articles.summary: Deputy leader Rachel Millward says two sectors planned for major North East expansion need changes.
articles.body:
The Green Party's deputy leader says a new generation of small nuclear power stations is not a solution to rising energy bills.

The government hopes to have a new generation of modular reactors up and running in the mid-2030s, including 12 planned for Hartlepool, but Rachel Millward told the BBC new nuclear still takes too long to develop.

Speaking ahead of her party's annual conference in Brighton, Millward also said the party was looking to pause the development of data centres to ensure they are built in more sustainable ways.

Work has already begun on a giant artificial intelligence campus at Cambois in Northumberland, while part of the Teesworks site has been earmarked for a data centre.

Restating the Green Party's commitment to wind and solar, Millward said: "The gap between greenlighting the [nuclear] project and actually getting the energy is huge.

"I think the most important thing is that we are investing in the most effective and fastest way, which is renewables, and that will be millions more jobs for people.

"That is the economy of the future, at the moment the green policy does not support nuclear."

Millward also said her party does not want to ban data centres but does want a temporary halt on their development to find the best way of making them work for the environment and communities.

"We need to do this in the most effective, sustainable and efficient way," she said.

"What we're seeing at the moment is at hyperscale and it's basically benefiting US tech giants rather than our communities.

"It's astonishing the amount of power they use. They're causing heat and noise for local communities.

"So we need to get the places for them right, the form right and the tech right."

Pressed on whether her party could win parliamentary seats in the North East at the next election, Millward said she was not revealing which constituencies the party was targeting at the moment.

But she claimed Green Party success had changed the direction of the country by unseating Keir Starmer and changing his party's policies.

She said: "The more Greens in parliament, the more Green-led councils there are, the more we push this Labour government in the right direction."

The BBC has been talking to leading political figures from the main parties ahead of their conferences.

articles.title: Zack Polanski to call for three-year cap on private rent rises
articles.summary: In his speech to his party's conference, the Green leader will frame housing as a key issue of generational fairness.
articles.body:
Zack Polanski is set to call for a three-year "emergency brake" on private rent increases when he opens the Green Party's conference later.

In his speech to party activists on Friday afternoon, the Green leader will seek to frame housing as a key issue of generational fairness.

He will urge the government to prevent private rents rising above whichever is lowest out of the consumer price index measure of inflation , wage growth or 2%, for three years.

According to the party, he will also argue pressure from the Greens has forced Labour into a change of political direction on some issues.

The Green Party of England and Wales is billing the gathering in Brighton as its biggest ever, after announcing earlier this year that its membership had tripled since Polanski's election as leader just over a year ago.

In his speech, Polanski is expected to say generations are having to live with their parents because of rent prices, from 19-year-olds commuting to university, 25-year-olds unable to find a job, to 35-year-olds moving back home with their partners.

"For too long, landlords have been able to hike prices way beyond wages, leaving renters forced to meet the cost to keep a roof over their heads, cutting back and back and back on everything else," he is expected to say.

A slowdown on private rent increases "would give renters vital breathing space" and give time for ministers to create a national Fair Rents Guarantee that keeps rents affordable for the future, he is expected to say.

Earlier this year, the government brought in the Renters' Rights Act under which landlords can only increase rent once a year to the property's open market rate.

Average UK monthly private rents increased by 3.5%, to £1,377, in the 12 months to January 2026, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The Act also means tenancies are rolling rather than fixed term, and makes it harder for landlords to evict tenants.

But Polanski is expected to argue it does not go far enough in ending "fear and uncertainty" for the millions of private renters in the UK.

The Institute for Fiscal Studies has previously warned that rent controls - an issue the Greens have long campaigned for - would result in "unintended consequences" including demand exceeding supply in the rental market.

Issues for Greens to grapple with at conference

The Green conference follows the party gaining hundreds of councillors earlier this year at England's local elections and its fifth MP, Hannah Spencer, in the Makerfield by-election.

But there are signs its rise in national polls may have stalled in recent months, while the party also faces questions over how to react to Labour's change of leadership under Andy Burnham.

Since Burnham became prime minister, Labour has shifted its stance in a number of areas where it had been in danger of being outflanked politically by the Greens.

In an interview ahead of the conference, the party's co-deputy leader Rachel Millward said Labour was now "rhetorically, on a much more similar ground" to her party.

This includes Burnham's move towards electoral reform , where the Greens have long demanded a shake-up of the Westminster voting system, and opening the door to a much closer future relationship with the European Union.

Labour has also announced sanctions on Israeli West Bank settlements deemed illegal under international law, and the reopening of a scheme to resettle refugees .

Speaking ahead of the conference, Polanski claimed those two policies were a result of the electoral pressure his party has applied to Labour.

The timing of the conference could, however, prove awkward for Polanski, who is standing for the Greens in next week's Holborn and St Pancras by-election triggered by Sir Keir Starmer's decision to leave Parliament .

Polanski said last week he was intending to come "straight back" to the central London seat after his leader's speech.

He has even urged the party's activists to leave the conference over the weekend to help him campaign.

Victory in the contest would give the Greens their first seat in the capital, but would require them to overturn a huge Labour majority from the last election in 2024. A full list of candidates can be found here .

articles.title: 2026 Asian Games: Tom Kim leads men's golf event seeking win to secure military service exemption
articles.summary: Tom Kim tops the men's leaderboard after the third round at the Asian Games as he seeks a gold medal that will significantly reduce the time he is required to spend in South Korea's military.
articles.body:
Tom Kim topped the men's leaderboard after the third round at the Asian Games as he seeks a gold medal that will significantly reduce the time he is required to spend in South Korea's military.

Having started two shots off the lead, Kim hit a brilliant five-under 65 that included five birdies and an eagle, taking him a stroke clear at 12 under par with one round to play.

Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of military service before the age of 28.

However the government rewards Asian Games gold medals and Olympic medals of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.

Athletes who have previously secured the exemption include former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who served for only three weeks in 2020 having won the Asian Games two years earlier.

Kim hurried from the Presidents Cup in the United States to tee off at the Kasugai Country Club in Japan, having to manage on just six hours of sleep and a 14-hour time difference.

The 24-year-old previously came close to securing an exemption at the Paris Olympics in 2024, finishing day one tied for third before ultimately finishing eighth.

Having looked visibly emotional after that result, Kim is now chasing another chance to stop military service stalling his promising career, which has already featured an Asian Tour order of merit crown and four PGA Tour titles.

The world number 32's lead would have been larger had he not missed birdie putts on the 14th and 18th holes, but he stands clear of Taiwan's Wang Wei-hsuan, who had led overnight, and Japan's Kazuki Higa going into day four.

The men's team event title offers another route for military exemption, with South Korea also topping the men's leaderboard by one stroke.

Gold in that event will exempt Tom Kim and SH Kim, 28, regardless of the individual result, but it would come too late for the third team member, Mun Do-yeob, who has already served.

"I think about it. It's so tough," SH Kim said of the possibility of military service.

"I am 100% nervous, for sure. It's a lot of pressure. I could stay on the PGA Tour (with a gold). That's my goal."

articles.title: Heckler interrupts Trump as mixed crowd reaction unfolds at Medinah
articles.summary: palinchak/Depositphotos President Donald J. Trump speaks at Medinah President Donald J. Trump attended the 2026 Presidents Cup on September 27 at Medinah Cou...
articles.body:
President Donald J. Trump speaks at Medinah

President Donald J. Trump attended the 2026 Presidents Cup on September 27 at Medinah Country Club in Illinois, where brief first tee remarks drew cheers, applause, opposition, and one interruption from spectators.

The appearance came before Sunday singles at the biennial golf event, after Air Force One flew over the course and security tightened around the first tee area west of Chicago.

President Donald J. Trump faces interruption

President Trump thanked the crowd and said media coverage would portray the reception poorly. At the same time, he told spectators that Medinah had given him a good response before the final session began.

A person in the upper grandstand shouted criticism during the opening remarks. Still, President Trump kept speaking and moved quickly toward golf, the players, and the requested short address for spectators.

President Donald J. Trump keeps remarks brief

President Trump said Brian Rolapp asked for brief remarks, then told fans they wanted golf instead of a lengthy speech before Sunday singles play began at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

Cameron Young and Ryo Hisatsune then opened singles from the first tee. Their pairing began the 12-match Sunday schedule at Medinah Country Club in Illinois, with the remaining matches to follow.

Brian Rolapp, the PGA Tour CEO, met President Trump at the first tee and introduced him before spectators near the trophy, microphones, grandstand, and player seating areas at Medinah Country Club.

The PGA Tour announced on August 29 that President Trump accepted the honorary chairman role, continuing a Presidents Cup custom tied to host country leaders during tournament week in Illinois.

Presidents Cup crowd gives mixed response

The Medinah crowd gave President Trump a mixed reception before Sunday singles, with loud cheers and USA chants alongside scattered boos and at least one interruption near the first tee.

Supporters grew louder during several moments, while opposing voices remained audible from parts of the stands. President Trump continued his remarks and responded to favorable sections with gestures nearby before play.

Medinah Country Club hosted the 16th Presidents Cup from September 24 through September 27, 2026. Practice days began earlier that week, before the four days of match play.

The event featured 12 U.S. golfers and 12 International Team members from outside Europe. Brandt Snedeker captained the United States, and Geoff Ogilvy led the opposing side at Medinah that week.

Presidents Cup format sets Sunday stakes

The 2026 Presidents Cup consisted of 30 matches across four competition days, using four-ball, foursomes, and singles formats. Thursday and Friday featured five matches each at Medinah Country Club.

Saturday added eight team contests before Sunday delivered 12 singles pairings. A win earned 1 point, while any tie after 18 holes gave each side 0.5 points under event scoring.

The International Team entered Sunday singles ahead 10.5-7.5 after building a three-point lead through team sessions, leaving the United States needing a final-day rally at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

Friday foursomes created the largest early swing, as the International Team won that session 5-0 and changed a 3-2 United States lead into a 7-3 deficit after two days of play.

United States completes Medinah comeback

The United States won the 2026 Presidents Cup 17-13 after earning 9.5 points from Sunday singles. The final session overturned the International Team's three-point overnight lead at Medinah Country Club.

The result gave the United States its 11th straight Presidents Cup victory. The streak continued after a closing day in which American players won most of the available singles points on Sunday.

President Donald J. Trump greets players

President Trump remained near the first tee after his remarks and greeted players from both teams as they arrived for Sunday singles at Medinah Country Club.

He watched the action between player introductions, signed hats for spectators, and later stayed for the trophy presentation, tying his visit to several parts of the final session at Medinah.

Fun fact: Medinah Country Club covers 640 acres , roughly a full square mile, and its clubhouse spans 120,000 square feet with a 60-foot-high rotunda.

Security procedures changed fan movement before President Trump arrived, with TSA-style screening and access restrictions around the first tee during the Presidents Cup' final session at Medinah Country Club.

Fans were advised to arrive early and expect extra travel time, while certain areas could be temporarily restricted or paused to support security operations before and during the event.

President Donald J. Trump holds event role

President Trump served as honorary chairman at Medinah, a ceremonial Presidents Cup role often linked to the host country's head of state during tournament week in the United States for 2026.

He previously held the same ceremonial position for the 2017 Presidents Cup at Liberty National, making Medinah his second appearance in that role for the competition across two presidential terms.

LIV Golf faces fresh uncertainty over a 2027 Open spot at St Andrews , with qualification rules potentially affecting players who lack separate exemptions into the championship field.

The Medinah appearance occurred during a live tournament, with a presidential visit, visible security, first-tee remarks, and a split crowd response before closing-day singles near Chicago, Illinois.

The scene remained tied to golf rather than a standalone speech, as Sunday singles proceeded, players moved through scheduled tee times, and organizers completed the event at Medinah Country Club.
