articles.title: Eagles’ new offense has players ‘second-guessing’ themselves: ‘It’s really frustrating’
articles.summary: The Eagles' offense is running into problems.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Eagles' new offensive scheme has not produced big results yet. That was especially true last week.

In the team's 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night , Philadelphia's offense was shut down, particularly in the second half. The Eagles gained 62 yards in the second half, with five of their drives ending in a punt, an interception or a failed fourth-down attempt.

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley gained 72 rushing yards in the first half, but he had only four carries for nine yards in the second half. Quarterback Jalen Hurts threw for only 153 yards and tossed an interception during the third quarter.

The Eagles brought in new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion this offseason with the goals of making the offense more efficient and dangerous by running a scheme that resembles the systems run by. Kyle Shanahan (San Francisco 49ers), Sean McVay (Los Angeles Rams and Matt LaFleur (Green Bay Packers).

Through the first three weeks of the season, Mannion has not delivered on either front. Are players still adapting, or is this situation more dire than that?

"It's just growing pains as far as we understand our system, but then we go out there and maybe they present a look that we weren't prepared for," Eagles' backup tight end Johnny Mundt told NJ.com. "And so it's like you got to trust your rules. You got to know your rules, which we do. It's just that you can't second-guess yourself and that second-guessing could lead to a false step or miss target on your hat, so to speak. So we'll get there."

The Eagles have scored zero points in the first quarter this season, and overall, Philadelphia's offense ranks 24th in passing, 23rd in points scored, and 24th in yards per game.

The Eagles rank 20th overall in offensive EPA/play (-0.052) and their production drops to 28th in offensive EPA/play (-0.218) during the second half of games.

Among the 32 NFL teams, the Eagles have the second-worst offensive success rate (29.5%) during the second half, only ahead of the Miami Dolphins in that category, according to RBSDM Stats.

"Run game, we line up with an unscouted look and it's like, 'Oh my gosh, there's a safety in between the backers,'" Mundt said as he further explained the Eagles' offensive struggles. "Just trust your rules. You hear the point. The next combination goes corresponding to that point. So again, trust your rules and just execute."

Philadelphia ranks 13th in rushing offense with 332 yards, but that figure is skewed by Hurts' 87 rushing yards.

Barkley was held to fewer than 100 rushing yards against both the Bears and the Commanders and only finished with nine yards against the Titans after suffering a stinger on the opening play.

"It's really frustrating knowing we put together a really good first half of football and maybe the scoreboard didn't show that for various different reasons, but we did a good job getting in and out of the huddle, doing all the basic stuff," Eagles center Drew Kendall told NJ.com about their struggles against the Bears. "And it led to big plays. So, yeah, it's frustrating when we can't keep that going. So, we need to figure out how we can do that."

Kendall said it's hard to tell whether the struggles stem from inexperience with the scheme or sloppy technique and poor fundamentals.

"Everyone in the offensive line room is their own biggest critic," Kendall said. "So everyone has stuff to get better on. We're also growing as a team. We're growing as an offense. We're trying to fully get to where we want to be. So it's a little bit of both."

Kendall does not want to blame the unscouted looks for their struggles.

"Every team's going to give you un-scouted looks, so it's our jobs to kind of identify that," Kendall said. "Sometimes that will mess up a play. You can't let that mess up a second play."

Most of the Eagles' offensive players have no prior experience playing in this type of scheme, but two of them are well-versed in it.

Wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks spent two years in Green Bay with Mannion, who was previously the Packers' quarterbacks coach.

"We getting there," Wicks said on Thursday. "Some stuff we got to clean up. There's a lot of stuff we got to clean up. You'll never be perfect, but everybody still getting adjusted to the new system, new scheme. That takes experience. When the bullets fly, it's full speed going against another team. That takes experience. And I think we working towards perfecting that. Even though I feel like nothing is perfect, but controlling our details and just like little things, little details and staying ahead of the sticks. That's in our control."

Mundt, a former teammate of Mannion on the Rams, has played in similar schemes during his entire 10-year career. From what he's seen, he believes the Eagles' offense will eventually gel.

"We're taking a lot of what they've done, had success here in the past, and morphing that into what Sean sees as the vision," Mundt said. "So, it's just making that concrete in our brains and just instilling those plays so we can run them in our sleep, so to speak."

The Eagles' offense will face more adversity moving forward. Starting tight end Dallas Goedert remains out with an MCL sprain, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith is unlikely to play against the Rams on Sunday due to a hamstring injury.

"It's tough to be rolling into game four and not [be] there yet just because we just want to get there now," Mundt said. "Now is always the best time."

articles.title: Peterborough appoint Forest Green boss Savage
articles.summary: Peterborough United appoint Forest Green Rovers boss Robbie Savage as Luke Williams' successor.
articles.body:
Peterborough United have appointed Forest Green Rovers boss Robbie Savage as their new manager.

The 51-year-old replaces Luke Williams at the Weston Homes Stadium after he was sacked on 19 September following a poor start to the League One season which has left Posh 23rd in the division.

Savage played as a midfielder for clubs including Derby County, Birmingham City, Leicester City and Blackburn Rovers.

He guided Forest Green to seventh in the National League last season but they were beaten in the play-off eliminators.

This season they sit 13th after 11 matches, with four wins, three draws and four defeats.

Former Wales international Savage was appointed by Forest Green in July last year, having previously managed fellow non-league side Macclesfield.

He will take charge of Peterborough for the first time when they host Ipswich Town Under-21s in the Jersey Mike's Trophy on 6 October, before Posh resume their league campaign with a trip to his former club Leicester on 10 October.

Savage, who has signed what Posh describe as a "long-term" contract, told the club's website he had been attracted to "the size of the club, the philosophy, working with young players and making them better".

He said: "I am really looking forward to getting out there on the training ground, but I am a manager - I will be there for every session, but I believe in trusting the coaches in delivering the messages and the session.

"I am not a manager who is going to want my teams to pass the ball around the back and chalk up 600 passes every game, we are going to go for it and attack and if we are 1-1 at home with five minutes to go, I want my teams to go for the winner.

"I understand there will be people out there with reservations. We all know the modern world has changed with social media. I understand it. I have been around for a long time. I will stand on that touchline and protect my players, it is a brilliant squad, I can't wait to get going, it is going to be fun."

Caretaker boss Ryan Harley will be Savage's assistant.

Chairman Darragh MacAnthony added: "Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager. A word I personally haven't used about our football club for too long.

"His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie. The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by."

Robbie Savage is an extremely surprising appointment for Peterborough United.

His managerial record to date is modest by League One standards and there are question marks over his ability to handle Darragh MacAnthony's famously hands-on style of ownership.

And yet, following two years of stasis, perhaps a Robbie Savage-shaped curveball is exactly what the Posh need?

Savage inherits a side sitting second from bottom of the League One table.

They have scored only four goals in the league so far this season - and only two of their past 23 league fixtures stretching back into last season. Key players have been sold and the summer replacements are yet to convince.

Savage will certainly need to hit the ground running. Job security has proved in short supply for recent Posh managers - with the notable exception of Darren Ferguson.

Luke Williams lasted nine months, Grant McCann the same. Steve Evans reached 10 months. Savage clearly has a huge task on his hands, but whatever happens - you get the feeling that it's unlikely to be dull.

articles.title: Si Woo Kim says Koivun never looked rattled during dramatic comeback
articles.summary: masuti/Shutterstock.com Si Woo Kim praises Jackson Koivun’s calm Si Woo Kim praised Jackson Koivun after their Sunday singles match at the 2026 Presidents Cu...
articles.body:
Si Woo Kim praises Jackson Koivun's calm

Si Woo Kim praised Jackson Koivun after their Sunday singles match at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club. Koivun rallied from 2 down through 10 holes and defeated Kim 2 up.

Koivun finished his Presidents Cup debut with a 2-0-1 record across three matches. The 21-year-old American earned 2.5 points and completed the week without a loss for the United States.

Kim said Koivun looked composed throughout their closing stretch and rarely appeared under pressure. The International Team player called his opponent a great rookie after watching him reverse the match late in the match.

Kim entered Sunday singles with three victories and one loss, making him one of the International Team's strongest performers. Koivun's comeback, therefore, came against an opponent who had already delivered three points.

Kim held a 2-up advantage after 10 holes, but Koivun changed the contest quickly. The American won Nos. 11, 12, and 13 in succession to take his first lead.

Koivun moved 2 up with a birdie at the 15th before Kim answered at No. 16. A final hole birdie gave Koivun the 2-up result and another United States point.

Koivun began his Presidents Cup debut alongside Justin Thomas in Thursday's fourball. The pair defeated Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria 4 and 3, giving the rookie an immediate point at Medinah.

Thomas and Koivun won five holes and lost one during that opening match. They closed the contest on the 15th after taking the final two holes with birdies at Nos. 14 and 15.

operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos

Koivun and Thomas returned together for Saturday's fourball against Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im. Their match ended in a tie, giving each team half a point before the final afternoon session.

The American pair led 2 up through 14 holes before Lee and Im responded. Lee won the 15th, and Im leveled the contest at No. 16 before both sides halved the remaining holes.

Jackson Koivun joins the Sunday comeback

Koivun's singles victory formed part of a large United States comeback on Sunday. The Americans entered the session trailing 10.5-7.5, then won 9.5 of 12 available points to finish 17-13.

Jacob Bridgeman delivered the clinching point by defeating Min Woo Lee 1 up. The victory secured an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup for the United States after the team began Sunday three points behind.

Jackson Koivun brings a Tour win to Medinah

Koivun arrived at Medinah months after winning the 3M Open in his third professional start. He finished 25 under at TPC Twin Cities and beat Scottie Scheffler by three strokes in July.

The 3M Open victory gave Koivun his first PGA Tour title and 500 FedExCup points. He also earned $1.584 million from the $8.8 million purse after closing with a 5 under 66.

Jackson Koivun leaves Auburn with records

Koivun turned professional in June 2026 after three seasons at Auburn University. He completed his college career with 11 individual wins and a 68.89 scoring average, both school records at Auburn.

His college resume also included NCAA team championships in 2024 and 2026. Koivun won Southeastern Conference Player of the Year honors three straight times and captured three consecutive SEC individual titles.

Jackson Koivun earns an accelerated path

Koivun earned a PGA Tour membership through the accelerated university pathway after reaching the required points threshold. He became the third player to qualify through that route before accepting membership after the 2026 U.S. Open.

His 2026 PGA Tour profile listed one victory, three top 10 finishes, and six made cuts in seven starts. Koivun also recorded four top 25 finishes during his first professional season.

Jackson Koivun posts strong Tour numbers

Koivun's 2026 PGA TOUR statistics included a 67.97 scoring average, 307.5 yards in driving distance, and a 73.70% greens-in-regulation rate. His statistics covered 540 holes.

He also recorded 1.583 strokes gained total and 0.691 strokes gained approaching the green. His putting average was 1.749, while his scrambling rate was 63.38%.

Fun fact: Koivun finished his Auburn career with 34 top 10 finishes in 39 starts, meaning he rarely wandered far from the leaderboard.

Jackson Koivun delivers in three matches

Medinah hosted the 16th Presidents Cup on Course No. 3. The venue had previously staged the 2012 Ryder Cup, two PGA Championships, and three U.S. Opens before hosting this team event.

Koivun did not play foursomes during the competition, so all 2.5 of his points came from four-ball and singles. His three appearances produced one win on Thursday, one tie on Saturday, and one Sunday victory.

The 2027 Ryder Cup qualification process begins with points available at The American Express in January. The top six eligible Americans after the BMW Championship will earn automatic places on the team.

U.S. Captain Jim Furyk will then make six captain selections during the week of August 30, 2027. Those choices will follow the Tour Championship and complete the 12-player American roster.

Scottie Scheffler shuts down recurring narrative about U.S. golf team , offering a player's perspective on how team chemistry and expectations shape American performance in international competition.

Jackson Koivun has no Ryder Cup guarantee

The 2027 Ryder Cup is scheduled for September 13 through 19 at Adare Manor in County Limerick, Ireland. Koivun would make his first Ryder Cup appearance if he qualifies or is selected.

His Presidents Cup performance does not guarantee a Ryder Cup place because qualification starts separately in 2027. Koivun will need qualifying points or a captain selection to join the United States team.

articles.title: Alfred Dunhill Links: Robert MacIntyre makes second-round move
articles.summary: Defending champion Robert MacIntyre shoots a second-round 65 to move into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, three strokes behind halfway leader Casey Jarvis of South Africa.
articles.body:
Alfred Dunhill Links Championship - round two

11 C Jarvis (RSA); -10 M Jordan (Eng), M. J. Daffue (RSA), R Repetto Taylor (Esp)

Selected others: -9 S Bairstow (Eng); -8 R MacIntyre (Sco), M Stewart (Sco), B Koepka (US), T Detry (Bel) -7 S Jamieson (Sco), C Syme (Sco) -6 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), T Fleetwood (Eng); - 5 L Donald (Eng) S Straka (Aus); -4 L Westwood (Eng), T Hatton (Eng), J Rose (Eng) +4 I Poulter (Eng)

Defending champion Robert MacIntyre took advantage of calm conditions at Kingsbarns to shoot 65 and charge into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

The Scot's round of seven under left him in a tie for ninth place, three strokes behind halfway leader Casey Jarvis of South Africa.

England's Matthew Jordan matched MacIntyre's score of 72 with six birdies and an eagle at Carnoustie to sit on 10 under for the tournament.

Spaniard Rocco Repetto Taylor is on the same mark, with his 64 at Kingsbarns the best round of the day.

"I was cleaning up the holes where I felt like you need to clean up, just kept it simple," MacIntyre told BBC Scotland.

"We got really got lucky with the weather, the last hole was the only one we had with the wind blowing up."

MacIntyre, who began the day on one under after his opening day at Carnoustie, reeled off four birdies on the front nine.

The Ryder Cup star was frustrated to drop a shot on the 11th but responded with four gains over the next five holes.

"I got wild with the bogey, but it spurs me on, three birdies in a row," added MacIntyre as he prepares to tee off at St Andrews on Saturday.

"[I'll] Just keep doing what I'm doing, shooting at pins, trusting the instincts."

Michael Stewart, the surprise first-round leader, was level with his compatriot after a 71 at Kingsbarns.

"Hopefully he can get that bit of luck over the weekend to get on here [DP World Tour] full-time," MacIntyre said of the world 979.

"I know the bits of luck I've had in my career that have got me to the position I'm in.

"His chipping and putting, I'm not sure there's many better on the whole planet."

American Brooks Koepka shot a 67 to join the Scottish pair on eight under, while English duo Tommy Fleetwood and Matt Fitzpatrick sit two shots behind the five-time Major champion.

In their first DP World Tour appearances in nearly four years, Lee Westwood got to four under after a 69 at Kingsbarns, but fellow LIV golfer Ian Poulter went out in 41 at Carnoustie on his way to 76 which left him four over.

articles.title: Sergio García solicita ante un tribunal la rescisión de su contrato con LIV Golf
articles.standfirst: El golfista español ha presentado una moción ante el tribunal de quiebras para que se rescinda formalmente su vínculo con la liga
articles.summary: El golfista español ha presentado una moción ante el tribunal de quiebras para que se rescinda formalmente su vínculo con la liga
articles.body: La situación en torno a LIV Golf 2.0 sigue siendo una incógnita pese a que el CEO de la competición, el estadounidense Scott O’Neil, anunciara un proyecto que incluía 10 torneos de cara a 2027. LIV Golf se vio obligado a declarar la bancarrota para así poder reestructurar el negocio con el apoyo financiero de BC Partners, pero el caso es que sigue sin ofrecer detalles de cómo avanzan las negociaciones con las diferentes partes. Los jugadores son esenciales en el proyecto y la solicitud de quiebra de LIV Golf en teoría los liberó de sus contratos. Por su parte, Sergio García ha presentado una moción ante el tribunal de quiebras para que se rescinda formalmente su contrato con LIV, con el fin de evitar confusiones sobre su disponibilidad para participar en torneos y de cara a los patrocinadores. En los documentos presentados por los abogados del golfista español, se afirma que la situación contractual actual con LIV Golf es confusa y podría impedirle intentar unirse a otro circuito o conseguir acuerdos comerciales mientras terceros no tengan claro si es agente libre o no. La liga que en su día impulsó Arabia Saudí se acogió al Capítulo 11 de la ley de quiebras de Estados Unidos y, como parte de la reestructuración para la versión 2.0, los contratos con los jugadores habrían quedado anulados. Sergio García busca el respaldo judicial antes de dar sus próximos pasos, como ya está haciendo también el campo que es sede de LIV Golf en Adelaida, que ha seguido el mismo camino que el castellonense para asegurar legalmente que está libre contractualmente. Deportivamente, la semana que viene veremos a García en Madrid donde disputará el Open de España presented by Madrid. Recordemos que 2027 es año Ryder y el DP World Tour podría recuperar las multas para quienes actúen en torneos de LIV Golf, como venía haciendo hasta este curso. Hace unos meses algunos jugadores alcanzaron un acuerdo para poder compaginar ambos circuitos sin ser multados, pero dicho acuerdo caduca a final de año.
